newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan sells end Apr diesel at below $25.50/bbl.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan sells end Apr diesel at below $25.50/bbl.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) sold by tender one 225,000--250,000-barrel cargo of 0.3 percent sulphur diesel at below $25.50 per barrel, for April 21-30 lifting, a CPC source said on Friday.
The cargo is for lifting from Kaohsiung, on a free-on board (fob) basis.
"The price was not very satisfactory," the source said. "One cargo is more than enough."
One trade source said the actual level awarded was $25.16 per barrel.
The source said the awarded level reflected the steeply backwardated market, as fob Singapore prices for early March is around $27.30 per barrel.
Traders were expecting prices to slip as about 500,000-700,000 tonnes of diesel from the West are expected to arrive to Asia in April.
They also said prices should slip from current high levels after a Singapore trader, who has purchased 2.32 million barrels over two weeks, completes his buying spree.
Diesel prices in Singapore has been hovering around $25.00 for about a month in January and February before it started to climb in end February when the Singapore trader emerged to buy.
